tb21_profile.skill: Understand the SQLite WAL on-disk binary format (header magic, page size, frame headers, checksums), repair a corrupted/tampered WAL so SQLite will replay it, and extract every committed record exactly
tb21_profile.domain: SQLite internals and WAL, database file-format parsing/repair, binary data recovery
tb21_profile.task_form: recover/repair-corrupted-data: fix a damaged binary DB artifact and emit exact records as JSON sorted by id

verifier_notes: TMax task_002015_30c1f280 (WAL recovery tool -> JSON) reads as an ideal match but is FREE per work/verifier_strength.json (single non-value test), so it is ranked in TMax per_source only, not final_top10. notes: CalibForge is a near-perfect match for this task and dominates final_top10 (7 of 10): it contains multiple SQLite-WAL-recovery tasks that reproduce the TB premise almost exactly — lost/lost-then-recover .db-wal, corrupted WAL header (magic + page size), checksum-mismatch frame dropping, records-missing-on-normal-query, and even the /app/recovered.json 'sorted by id, recover all N records' output format — and they are strongly verified. This is the clearest case in my five tasks where the new corpora beat the old pool outright. TMax is a solid second: a deep bench of WAL-replay/recovery tasks (SQLite and custom KV/C++), though only task_001233 and task_002461 are truly SQLite-WAL; its ideal-looking task_002015 is FREE and excluded. Terminal-Lego contributes real value via task_14420 (SQLite WAL checkpoint) plus several WAL-file-management tasks that teach the -wal/-shm layout. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has SQLite construction/dump tasks (one shares the dump-to-JSON output) but no WAL-corruption recovery, all absent-verifier. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have essentially nothing on WAL binary recovery; their best offerings are SQLite-schema-migration/Parquet-roundtrip/corrupted-scheduler-DB library fixes, all overall 1-2 and effectively filler — the merge step should not expect real transfer from them. No FREE candidate is in final_top10.
